FigureS2: Figure S2. Reported base qualities and observed control mismatch rates, related to Figure 2

A reported base quality is a prediction, and this is how far it holds at each of the four nanopore loci. Top, the mismatch rate measured in the AID-null controls, grouped into two-quality-score bins holding at least 2,000 bases after germline positions are excluded. Shading, 95% Clopper–Pearson intervals; downward triangles, bins with no mismatch, drawn at the upper confidence bound because a rate of zero cannot be placed on a logarithmic axis; dashed line, the error probability the quality score nominally implies, 10^{−Q/10}. Bottom, the number of control bases in each bin. Observations thin out above Q40, so the uncertainty grows there. This is why each locus is calibrated against its own controls rather than against the reported qualities. Experimental details: the J_{H}4 libraries were sequenced under order DHJGKB and the N114 V_{H} libraries under order 75K3B3; for Sμ and *Pim1* (PRJNA1481264) the deposited records do not establish which libraries shared a flow cell.
FigureS4_fdr_calibration: Figure S4. The control-based false-discovery threshold against planted truth, related to Figure 3

The spike-in libraries of Figure 3 (60 substitutions planted into 1–20 reads of each held-out AID-null control, three draws per control; 9 libraries per locus) were called at six target false-discovery rates, every other setting at its default and only the other controls serving as null and decoys. (A) Realised false-discovery proportion, false over all calls pooled across a locus's libraries, against the target; dashed line, agreement; shading, over target; a pooled proportion of zero is drawn on the 0 row. (B) False calls per library. (C) Recall of planted substitutions. Vertical lines, the default target of 5%. At the default, pooled proportions were 3.5–5.5% (1.6–2.6 false calls per library), and single libraries reached 10.6%. Below 5%, false calls levelled off at 0.2–1.2 per library while recall fell, consistent with library-specific errors that the other controls do not share and with decoy counts too coarse to resolve small targets (STAR Methods). The realised proportion depends on the number of true mutations per library (here 60) and is not a per-library guarantee. Analysis in `crm/spikein.py` (`--tag _fdrcal`) and `crm/figs/figS4_fdr_calibration.py`. Zero is retained at zero on a symmetric-log vertical axis, linear to 1% and logarithmic above it.
FigureS5_controls: Figure S5. How many AID-null controls, and which, related to Figure 3

Everything the read-library route does rests on the controls, so their number and their provenance were varied through the whole `run_project` procedure. J_{H}4: the case is KO1 carrying planted polyclonal lineages, or none; the controls are halves of KO2 and KO3, so the third and fourth are technical partitions of the same two animals rather than new mice; 10 repeats per setting; points, repeats; bars, means. (A) Recall of planted mutations by number of controls. With one control there are no decoys and the threshold falls back to Benjamini–Hochberg (BH), which is why recall drops: the empirical threshold needs a control to hold out. (B) False calls per library in lineage-bearing (filled) and all-null (open) libraries; above, the pooled false-discovery proportion of the lineage-bearing libraries. No all-null library produced a call at any number of controls. (C) One control carrying recurrent artifacts at six positions in 6% of its reads, with the noisy-control rule off and on, beside the clean set. The rule set the noisy control aside in 10 of 10 runs and a clean control in 2–3; with four controls and the rule on, one of 10 all-null libraries produced a call. Two controls are the point at which the procedure works as intended, and a third adds little. Controls from a different experiment were also tested, on Sμ: each LPS AID-null library, carrying 60 planted substitutions in three draws, was called against its own experiment's other two AID-null controls, against two or three AID-null controls from the CH12 experiment of the same BioProject, or against all five. Recall was 63% with matched controls and 66–68% with CH12 controls, at false-discovery proportions of 5.5% and 5.4–5.6%; pooling all five lowered false calls from 2.2 to 0.8 per library. The SRA reads carry no run identifiers, so that comparison is between experiments rather than between verified sequencing runs. Analysis in `crm/controls_design.py` and `crm/figs/figS5_controls.py`.
FigureS6_titration: Figure S6. Real hypermutation diluted into AID-null reads, related to Figure 3

Each AID-active library (donor) was mixed with one AID-null library (diluent) at 1–100% donor reads in 500 usable reads, 3 draws per fraction, and called against the other two AID-null libraries (J_{H}4: donors Wt2–Wt4, diluent KO1, controls KO2 and KO3; N114 V_{H}: donors C1, D3 and D5, diluent D1, controls C3 and C4). Unlike the planted mutations of Figure 3, these are the mutations AID itself made, carrying their own clonality, hotspot clustering and multiple mutations per read. Small faint markers, the individual draws; large markers, their mean; lines join consecutive fractions that produced calls and stop where calling does. Draws that called nothing cannot be placed on a logarithmic axis and are drawn as open markers in the "no call" strip below the break. (A, B) Observed mutation frequency against the frequency expected from donor and diluent alone; dashed line, equality, spanning the called points it refers to. Frequency is read-weighted, so its expectation is linear in the donor fraction. On N114 V_{H} frequency was 0.87–0.97 of the expected value at 25–50% donor reads. (C, D) Unique mutations called against the share of donor reads. Calling is a step rather than a fade: on J_{H}4 it began at 2% donor reads for Wt3 and 50% for Wt2, tracking how many reads carry each mutation, which is mutation load crossed with clonal structure. A control-based threshold admits no call until enough candidates exceed the controls' background, so a donor whose mutations sit on few reads each loses them all at once. With 3 draws per fraction these thresholds are coarse. N114 V_{H} ran with `ancestral_reference` (STAR Methods); under the default ≥50% rule a mutation fixed within a subclone is removed at full strength but counted once diluted, and D3 then read 1.84 per 10^{3} bp at 50% donor reads against 0.63 at 100%. Analysis in `crm/titration.py` and `crm/figs/figS6_titration.py`.
FigureS7_indels: Figure S7. Indels planted into held-out AID-null libraries, related to Figure 3

The indel counterpart of Figures 3A and 3B. Ten insertions or deletions of 1–40 bp were planted into the reads of a held-out AID-null library, eight draws per control, 240 planted indels per amplicon, each carried by a set number of reads; error models were fitted to the other controls (STAR Methods). (A) Recall by the number of reads carrying the indel. Small faint markers, the three held-out controls in their own right. Recall below the three-read floor is zero by definition rather than by measurement (`indel_min_reads`), so those counts are drawn open, on the shading, and the line starts at three reads instead of running through them. Legend, recall of the indels carried by three or more reads; above the panel, the false calls each cost. (B) Recall by indel class among the events carried by three or more reads; beside each bar, the planted events of that class, several of which are few enough that the proportion is coarse. Single-base deletions inside a homopolymer are the class nanopore recovers least reliably, which is the error mode the indel model is fitted against. On J_{H}4 the false calls are not eight events but one: the same 28-bp deletion, in the same four reads of one control, in every draw. It carries 5-bp microhomology at its ends, so it is most likely a molecule the material already held rather than a calling error. Analysis in `crm/indel_spike.py` and `crm/figs/figS7_indels.py`.
FigureS8_estimates: Figure S8. Single-read estimate, power and UMI consensus, related to Figure 3

Four checks on what the read-library route can and cannot resolve. (A) Change in the aggregate single-read estimate against one-read mutations planted into held-out J_{H}4 control libraries (three controls; three replicates per amount); dashed line, identity. (B) Power at α = 0.05, two-sided, from the Welch test on log rates, by animals per group and by the size of the difference sought, simulated from the J_{H}4 wild-type pilot (3 mice, 500 reads each; 1,000 experiments per point; negative-binomial counts with the pilot's clumping, animals log-normal with the pilot's between-animal coefficient of variation, CV 0.95). Dotted line, 80% power. How many animals are needed depends on the difference being sought, not on the method alone: a 2-fold difference between two AID-proficient groups needs about 24 per group at this CV, whereas at 10-fold three animals give 63% power and five give 97%, and at 50-fold three give 97%. The comparisons this paper makes are AID-competent against AID-null and run 38–141-fold, which is why they separate at three animals per group. The CV is itself estimated from three mice and so is the loosest term in the calculation. (C) Simulated UMI libraries built from real control reads, three held-out controls each: false calls per library when every read is used and when reads are first collapsed to a consensus by tag. The four conditions are the two amplicons under two planted mutation loads: J_{H}4 polyclonal (about 40 clones) and J_{H}4 low load, and N114 V_{H} subclonal (one dominant clone) and N114 V_{H} low load, the same scenarios as Figure S25A. Consensus removes every false call in three of the four and leaves 0.67 in the fourth, annotated on the panel because a zero-height bar cannot be told from a missing one, while recall of the planted mutations rises from 90–96% to 99–100%. The two AID-null conditions are not plotted; their false calls fall from 0.67 and 2.67 per library to zero. Grouping reads by tag leaves 165 molecules from the 500 reads analysed, so the gain is bought with depth. (D) The same question on real data: error remaining after consensus in dual-UMI R10 reads of rRNA operons[@karst2021], by the number of reads per molecule; n, molecules; dashed line, the error of the raw reads; diamond, all 103 molecules of three or more reads pooled, with a bootstrap 95% interval from 2,000 resamples of molecules at fixed raw error. Consensus reduced error 57-fold, and at ten or more reads per molecule the residual substitution error approached one base in 10,000; what remains is mostly homopolymer indels. These are rRNA operons, not an SHM experiment: the panel measures what consensus does to sequencing error, which is why it sits beside the simulation in C rather than among the AID datasets of Figure 7.

FigureS10: Figure S10. Sequencing depth and unique-variant discovery, related to Figure 4

Every library was analyzed at 30–1,000 reads, and the whole analysis was repeated five times at each depth with a different random draw of usable reads, the AID-null controls redrawn and recalibrated at that depth each time, so the spread shown is the spread a single run would have had. (A and B) J_{H}4 unique variants and unique-variant density against depth; (C and D) the same for N114 V_{H}. Points, the five draws of each library; lines, their mean; blue, AID-active libraries, red, AID-null. A library with no calls has a density of zero, which has no logarithm: those draws are drawn on the "0" row below the dotted break rather than floored to a small number, and they are common (J_{H}4 KO1 and KO3 called nothing at any depth in any draw). Density falls with depth because its numerator, distinct calls, saturates while its denominator keeps growing, so a density is only comparable at a stated depth. (E) How much of each AID-active library's own variant set each depth recovered. The denominator is the most that library ever yielded, over every depth and every draw, so a library is read against its own discovery rather than against its 1,000-read value alone; lines, the range of five draws; vertical line, the 500 reads used throughout. Discovery rises steeply and then flattens, as further reads re-sample positions already seen rather than revealing new ones, which is what saturation looks like for a finite set of truly mutated positions. The J_{H}4 libraries are near their own total by 500 reads (90% on average), whereas the N114 V_{H} libraries, which carry fewer mutations, are still climbing (59%). At 30 reads one draw is not informative: J_{H}4 Wt2 gave between 7 and 60 calls across its five draws, against 212 to 244 at 500 reads.
FigureS12_immcantation: Figure S12. SHMtrace and the IgBLAST–SHazaM route on the same N114 V_{H} reads, related to Figure 4

The 500 reads SHMtrace analyzed from each N114 V_{H} library were assigned by IgBLAST (IGHV1-47-36*01; the parental line is 99.3% identical to it over 294 bp) and their substitutions over the V segment counted by SHazaM, with the IMGT germline, with the parental V segment as germline, and with the parental germline after masking bases below Q20; SHMtrace's calls over the same segment are shown for comparison. (A) Mutation frequency per library; filled, pMX-*Aicda*; open, empty vector; triangles, libraries with no SHMtrace call, drawn at one event; bars, geometric means. (B) Geometric-mean separation of pMX-*Aicda* from empty-vector libraries. The SHazaM routes count every substitution in every read, including real single-read mutations that SHMtrace does not call, so their AID-library values are higher (2.8 against 1.6 per 10^{3} bp with masking); their empty-vector values (4.22 and 0.09 per 10^{3} bp without and with the parental germline and masking) are the background they cannot remove. MiXCR was not run. Analysis in `crm/immcantation_compare.py` and `crm/figs/figS12_immcantation.py`.

FigureS24: Figure S24. End-to-end stress tests using resampled control reads, related to STAR Methods

AID-null J_{H}4 reads were resampled and analyzed with `run_project`, including margin selection, decoy thresholding and noisy-control exclusion. Cases used KO1. Two-control analyses used one partition each from KO2 and KO3; three-control analyses used two KO2 partitions and one KO3 partition. Case and control read records did not overlap. These are conditional resampling experiments using existing libraries, rather than independent preparations or a new sequencing run. Unless stated otherwise, analyses used three controls and 500 reads. Teal, exclusion enabled; amber, exclusion disabled, paired on identical inputs. (A) All-null resamples with any call and 95% Clopper–Pearson intervals; n = 25 per setting for unmodified background and one noisy control, and n = 5 for case-only and shared artifacts. Any discovery gives an all-null false-discovery proportion (FDP) of 1. (B) Mean false calls ± SEM. (C) Individual FDPs in mutation-bearing resamples, five per condition and setting; black bars, means; dashed line, nominal 5% target. (D) Exclusion rate under a heterogeneous null; n = 5 per setting with two controls at 250 or 1,000 reads, and n = 25 with three controls at 500 reads. Artifacts occupied six positions with nominal 6% support at each. Shared artifacts used identical alternate alleles and avoided planted biological mutations. Injection preserved read orientation and quality order. Shared all-null artifacts produced calls in 0/5 resamples with exclusion enabled and 0/5 disabled, versus 5/5 in both case-only settings. Small resample counts limit conclusions about error control (STAR Methods).
